316046.title: Carmichael's totient function conjecture
316046.statement:
For a positive integer $n$ let

$$
\varphi(n) = \#\{k : 1 \le k \le n,\ \gcd(k,n) = 1\}
$$

be Euler's totient function, and for a positive integer $f$ let

$$
A(f) = \#\{n \ge 1 : \varphi(n) = f\}
$$

be the multiplicity of $f$ as a value of $\varphi$.

For every integer $n \ge 1$ there exists an integer $m \ne n$, $m \ge 1$, with

$$
\varphi(m) = \varphi(n).
$$

Equivalently, $A(f) \ne 1$ for every positive integer
$f$; that is, no value attained by $\varphi$ is attained by exactly one
argument.

316050.title: Grimm's conjecture
316050.statement:
For positive integers $n$ and $k$, if the $k$ consecutive integers $n+1, n+2,
\dots,
n+k$ are all composite, then there exists a sequence of distinct prime numbers $\left(p_{i}\right)_{i=1}^{k}$
such that $p_{i}$ divides $n+i$ for every $1 \leq i \leq k$.

A weaker assertion: for positive integers $n$ and $k$, if no prime lies in the
interval $[n+1, n+k]$, then

$$
\prod_{1\,\leq\,x\,\leq\,k}(n+x)
$$

has at least $k$ distinct prime divisors.

316055.title: Newman's conjecture
316055.statement:
For a nonnegative integer $n$, let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of
$n$, i.e. the number of ways of writing $n$ as a sum of positive integers
without regard to order, with the convention $p(0)=1$, so that

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} p(n)q^{n} = \prod_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1-q^{k}}.
$$

For every integer $m \ge 1$ and every integer $r$ with $0 \le r \le m-1$, the
set

$$
\{\, n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \;:\; p(n) \equiv r \pmod{m} \,\}
$$

is infinite.

316056.title: Scholz conjecture
316056.statement:
For a positive integer $x$, an addition chain for $x$ is a finite sequence of
positive integers

$$
a_0 = 1,\; a_1,\; a_2,\; \dots,\; a_r = x
$$

such that for every $k$ with $1 \le k \le r$ there exist indices $i, j$ with $0
\le i, j \le k-1$ (possibly $i = j$) satisfying $a_k = a_i +
a_j$. The length of such a chain is $r$, the number of sums performed, and
$l(x)$ denotes the least length of an addition chain for $x$, i.e.

$$
l(x) = \min\{r : \text{there is an addition chain } 1 = a_0, a_1, \dots, a_r = x\}.
$$

For every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$
l(2^n - 1) \le n - 1 + l(n).
$$

316057.title: Singmaster's conjecture
316057.statement:
For an integer $a>1$, let

$$
N(a)=\#\left\{(n,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{2}\;:\;0\le k\le n,\ \binom{n}{k}=a\right\},
$$

the number of positions in Pascal's triangle at which the entry equals
$a$ (each occurrence in a row being counted separately, so that e.g. $\binom{n}{k}$
and $\binom{n}{n-k}$ count as two occurrences when $k\neq
n-k$). Note that $N(a)$ is finite for every $a>1$, since $\binom{n}{k}=a$ forces
$n\le a$.

There exists a natural number $M$ such that

$$
N(a)\le M\qquad\text{for all integers } a>1;
$$

equivalently, $N(a)=O(1)$.

316077.title: Kummer–Vandiver conjecture
316077.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $\zeta_p$ be a primitive $p$-th root of unity, and
let

$$
K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^{+} = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p + \zeta_p^{-1})
$$

be the maximal real subfield of the
$p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$. Let
$h_K$ denote the class number of $K$, i.e. the order of the ideal class group of
the ring of integers of $K$; equivalently, $h_K =
h_2$ is the second factor in the decomposition $h = h_1
h_2$ of the class number $h$ of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$, where $h_2 =
h_K$ and $h_1 = h/h_K$.

Then

$$
p \nmid h_K
$$

for every odd prime $p$.

316111.title: Pillai's conjecture
316111.statement:
Call an integer $p$ a perfect power if $p = x^n$ for some integers $x \ge
1$ and $n \ge 2$, and let $p_1 < p_2 < p_3 <
\cdots$ be the increasing enumeration of the perfect powers $\ge 1$. Then

$$
\lim_{k \to \infty} (p_{k+1} - p_k) = \infty;
$$

equivalently, every positive integer is representable in only finitely many ways
as a difference of two perfect powers. More generally, for all fixed positive
integers $A$, $B$, $C$, the set of quadruples $(x, y, m, n)$ of integers with

$$
x \ge 1, \quad y \ge 1, \quad m \ge 2, \quad n \ge 2, \quad (m,n) \neq (2,2),
$$

satisfying

$$
A x^n - B y^m = C
$$

is finite.

316114.title: Agoh–Giuga conjecture
316114.statement:
Let the Bernoulli numbers $B_k \in \mathbb{Q}$ be defined by

$$
\frac{t}{e^{t}-1}=\sum_{k\ge 0}B_{k}\frac{t^{k}}{k!}.
$$

For an integer $p>1$ the rational number $pB_{p-1}$ has denominator prime to
$p$, so the congruence $pB_{p-1}\equiv -1 \pmod
p$ is meaningful, meaning that the numerator of $pB_{p-1}+1$ written in lowest
terms is divisible by $p$.

For every integer $p>1$,

$$
p \text{ is prime} \iff pB_{p-1}\equiv -1 \pmod{p},
$$

and equivalently, for every integer $p>1$,

$$
p \text{ is prime} \iff \sum_{i=1}^{p-1} i^{\,p-1}\equiv -1 \pmod{p}.
$$

316115.title: Agrawal's conjecture
316115.statement:
Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers with $\gcd(n,r)=1$, and consider the
congruence

$$
(X-1)^{n}\equiv X^{n}-1 \pmod{n,\;X^{r}-1},
$$

meaning that the two polynomials $(X-1)^{n}$ and $X^{n}-1$ have the same image
in the ring
$(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[X]/(X^{r}-1)$, i.e. every coefficient of $(X-1)^{n}-(X^{n}-1)$,
after reduction of exponents modulo $r$ via $X^{r}=1$, is divisible by $n$.

For every such pair $(n,r)$ satisfying this congruence, either $n$ is prime or

$$
n^{2}\equiv 1 \pmod{r}.
$$

316121.title: Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture
316121.statement:
Call a positive integer $m$ *powerful* if for every prime $p$ with $p \mid m$
one also has $p^{2} \mid m$; equivalently, $m$ is powerful if and only if $m =
a^{2}b^{3}$ for some positive integers $a,
b$. Writing the prime factorization as $m=\prod_i
p_i^{\alpha_i}$, this says that $\alpha_i \geq 2$ for every $i$.

For every integer $n \geq 1$, the three consecutive integers $n$, $n+1$,
$n+2$ are not all powerful; that is, there is no $n \geq
1$ such that each of $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$ satisfies the condition that every prime
dividing it divides it at least twice.

316122.title: Feit–Thompson conjecture
316122.statement:
For distinct primes $p$ and $q$, set

$$
N_{p,q} \;=\; \frac{p^{q}-1}{p-1} \;=\; 1 + p + p^{2} + \cdots + p^{q-1}, \qquad N_{q,p} \;=\; \frac{q^{p}-1}{q-1} \;=\; 1 + q + q^{2} + \cdots + q^{p-1},
$$

both of which are positive integers. Then for every pair of distinct primes
$p$ and $q$,

$$
\frac{p^{q}-1}{p-1} \;\nmid\; \frac{q^{p}-1}{q-1};
$$

that is, there exists no integer $k$ with $N_{q,p} = k\,N_{p,q}$.

316130.title: New Mersenne conjecture
316130.statement:
For an odd natural number $p$ consider the following three conditions:

(i) there is a natural number $k$ such that $p = 2^k + 1$, $p = 2^k - 1$, $p =
4^k + 3$, or $p = 4^k - 3$;

(ii) $2^p - 1$ is prime;

(iii) $(2^p + 1)/3$ is prime (note that $3 \mid 2^p + 1$ for every odd $p$, so
this quotient is an integer).

For every odd natural number
$p$, if at least two of the conditions (i), (ii), (iii) hold for $p$, then all
three hold for $p$.

316142.title: Bing–Borsuk conjecture
316142.statement:
For a metric space $M$, say that $M$ is *homogeneous* if for any two points
$m_1,m_2\in M$ there is a homeomorphism of $M$ onto itself taking $m_1$ to
$m_2$.

Say that a metric space
$M$ is an *absolute neighborhood retract* (ANR) if for every closed embedding $f:M\rightarrow
N$ into a metric space $N$ there exists an open neighbourhood $U$ of $f(M)$ in
$N$ that retracts onto $f(M)$, i.e. there is a continuous map
$r:U\rightarrow f(M)$ with $r\restriction f(M)=\mathrm{id}_{f(M)}$.

Say that $M$ is an *$n$-manifold* if every point of
$M$ has an open neighbourhood homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Let $n\geq 1$ and let
$M$ be a metric space which is homogeneous, is an ANR, and has topological dimension $\dim
M=n$. Then $M$ is an $n$-manifold.

316143.title: Borel conjecture
316143.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be closed topological manifolds that are aspherical, i.e.
connected with $\pi_n(M)=\pi_n(N)=0$ for all $n\ge 2$ (equivalently, with
contractible universal covers). Then every homotopy equivalence

$$
f\colon M\to N
$$

is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

In particular, if $M$ and $N$ are closed aspherical topological manifolds with
$\pi_1(M)\cong\pi_1(N)$, then $M$ and $N$ are homeomorphic.

316154.title: Torsion conjecture
316154.statement:
For a number field $K$ and an abelian variety $A$ over $K$, let $A(K)$ denote
the group of $K$-rational points of $A$ and let

$$
A(K)_{\mathrm{tors}} = \{P \in A(K) : nP = 0 \text{ for some integer } n \ge 1\}
$$

be its torsion subgroup, which is finite since $A(K)$ is a finitely generated
abelian group.

For every pair of integers $g \ge 1$ and $d \ge 1$ there exists a constant
$C(g,d) < \infty$ such that

$$
\#A(K)_{\mathrm{tors}} \le C(g,d)
$$

for every number field $K$ with $[K:\mathbb{Q}] =
d$ and every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ with $\dim A =
g$; that is, the bound depends only on $g$ and on the degree
$d$, and not otherwise on $A$ or on $K$.

316814.title: The infinitude of primes of level $(1;i)$
316814.statement: Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime, and let level $(1;i)$ be the level notation used in the paper's decomposition. **Level-$(1;i)$ infinitude conjecture.** For every integer $i\ge 1$, the number of primes of level $(1;i)$ is infinite. The case $i=1$ is identified with the conjecture that infinitely many balanced primes exist; the generalization is proposed without a proof.

317184.title: Non-finite generation of nonuniform lattices in right-angled hyperbolic buildings
317184.statement: Let $X$ be a right-angled hyperbolic building, let $G=\operatorname{Aut}(X)$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonuniform lattice in $G$. **Non-finite generation conjecture.** The group $\Gamma$ is not finitely generated. This extends the corresponding result for trees and is known for many nonuniform lattices in right-angled hyperbolic buildings, but the assertion for every such lattice remains open.

317917.title: Generalized manifolds resolution conjecture
317917.statement: Let $X$ be a generalized $n$-manifold with $n\geq 3$. **Generalized manifolds resolution conjecture.** The space $X$ has a resolution. The conjecture is false in higher dimensions: non-resolvable generalized $n$-manifolds are known for every $n\geq 6$.

318237.title: The conjecture that finite Poincaré complexes are manifolds up to homotopy
318237.statement: A finite Poincaré complex is a finite complex satisfying Poincaré duality. **Aspherical Poincaré complexes conjecture.** Every finite Poincaré complex is homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold. The claim asks whether Poincaré duality alone, together with finiteness, is sufficient for homotopy realization by a closed manifold.

318493.title: Linearity conjecture for free-by-cyclic groups
318493.statement:
Let $F$ be a free group and let

$$
\Gamma=F\rtimes\mathbb Z.
$$

Equivalently, consider an exact sequence

$$
1 \to F \to \Gamma \to \mathbb Z \to 1.
$$

**Free-by-cyclic linearity conjecture.** The group $\Gamma$ is linear. This extends the paper’s corollary for extensions of $F_2$ by $\mathbb Z$ to arbitrary free groups; the source presents it as suggested by those preceding linearity results.

318577.title: The improved Legendre conjecture
318577.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $p$ and $q$ denote primes. **The improved Legendre conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there exist at least two primes $p$ and $q$ satisfying

$$
n^{2}<p<q<(n+1)^{2}.
$$

This strengthens Legendre's conjecture by asserting that every interval between consecutive squares contains at least two primes; the source supports it only with empirical observations.

319162.title: Astala's conjecture on the sharp dimension of quasicircles
319162.statement:
Let $0<k<1$, and let a **$k$-quasicircle** be a quasicircle with parameter $k$. **Astala's conjecture.** There exists a $k$-quasicircle $\Gamma$ with Hausdorff dimension

$$
\dim \Gamma=1+k^2.
$$

Astala's upper estimate $\dim\Gamma\leq 1+k^2$ is known, while the conjecture asks for sharpness, namely attainment of the bound for every $0<k<1$.

319274.title: Shevelev's bound for the normalized maximal minor increment
319274.statement:
Write

$$
\rho^{(i)}=\lambda_i n_{i-1},\qquad \lambda_i\geq1.
$$

A **normalized-increment bound conjecture** asserts that, for every $i\geq6$,

$$
\lambda_i\leq\frac54.
$$

The paper uses this proposed bound to derive the stated sufficient condition for infinitely many twin primes; the supplied source does not establish the bound.

319700.title: The torus level-set length bound in dimension two
319700.statement:
Let $g$ be a metric on the two-dimensional torus $T^2$, and let $f:T^2\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$. **Naive conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, for every $y\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
\operatorname{Length}\bigl[f^{-1}(y)\bigr]\leq C\operatorname{Area}(T^2,g)^{1/2}.
$$

The source states that this conjecture is true and attributes the result to Balacheff and Sabourau.

319701.title: The torus level-set area bound in dimension three
319701.statement:
Let $g$ be a metric on the three-dimensional torus $T^3$, and let $f:T^3\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$. **Naive conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, for every $y\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
\operatorname{Area}\bigl[f^{-1}(y)\bigr]\leq C\operatorname{Vol}(T^3,g)^{2/3}.
$$

The source explicitly says that this conjecture is wrong and that counterexamples are based on work of Brooks.

319785.title: The optimal exponential bound conjecture for the arithmetic function f
319785.statement:
Let $f$ be the arithmetic function defined earlier in the paper. **Optimal exponential bound conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
\prod_{r=1}^{n} f(r)<4^n.
$$

This conjecture would improve the preceding bound $\prod_{r=1}^{n}f(r)\leq c^n$ and is described by the authors as very probably true, although they state that proving or disproving it seems difficult.

320608.title: Gross's nonsolvable extensions conjecture
320608.statement: Let $p$ be a prime. **Gross's conjecture.** For every prime $p$, there exists a nonsolvable Galois number field $K$ ramified only at $p$. This conjecture concerns the existence of number fields with minimal ramification and is linked to Hilbert modular forms through their associated Galois representations. The source attributes it to Gross and does not state a resolution.

321201.title: The prime-index irreducibility conjecture for Stern polynomials
321201.statement:
Let $B_p(t)$ be the Stern polynomial indexed by a prime number $p$. **The prime-index irreducibility conjecture.** For every prime number $p$, the polynomial $B_p(t)$ is irreducible.

The conjecture was checked computationally for the first million primes, but the supplied text gives no general proof or resolution.

321486.title: Surjectivity conjecture for the generic-point cycle class map
321486.statement:
Let $X/{\mathbb C}$ be a smooth projective variety, and let $r,m\geq 0$. Write $\lim(\textup{cl}_{r,m})$ for the direct-limit cycle class map at the generic point of $X$.

**Generic-point cycle class conjecture.** For all $r,m\geq 0$, statement (S3) holds. The supplied span does not reproduce statement (S3), so its precise mathematical content cannot be determined from the available context.

321986.title: The Hessian rank conjecture for Coxeter arrangements of types E6, E7, and E8
321986.statement: Let $\mathsc{A}$ be the Coxeter arrangement associated with a finite reflection group $W$. The **Hessian rank conjecture.** The Hessian rank condition holds for $\mathsc{A}$ if $W$ is of type $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$. Computing limitations leave this conjecture open for these exceptional types; the preceding theorem establishes the Hessian rank condition for all other types considered in the paper.

322170.title: The Bocci-Harbourne-Essential containment conjecture
322170.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, let $R=K[\mathbb{P}^{N}]$, and let $I\subseteq R$ be a homogeneous ideal. **Bocci-Harbourne-Essential conjecture.** For every $r$,

$$
I^{(rN-(N-1))}\subseteq I^r.
$$

The statement is the proposed optimal improvement of the general $I^{(rN)}\subseteq I^r$ containment; the source attributes it to the cited authors and gives no evidence of resolution.

322943.title: Non-algebraicity conjecture for rational-function composition generating functions
322943.statement:
Let $m>2$, let $p(z)\in\mathbb N(z)$ be a rational function with $p(1)>1$, and let $D(z)$ denote the generating function under consideration for the corresponding restricted compositions.

**Non-algebraicity conjecture.** The generating function $D(z)$ is not algebraic.

The claim is known for all odd $m>2$, while the paper reports no general proof for even $m>2$.

322973.title: Weak SHGH conjecture for nef linear systems
322973.statement: Let $X_n$ be the blow-up of the projective plane at $n$ general points, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a **nef** linear system, meaning that $\mathcal{L}\cdot\mathcal{L}'\geq0$ for every effective linear system $\mathcal{L}'$. **Weak SHGH conjecture.** The linear system $\mathcal{L}$ is not special. This is presented as a weak form of the SHGH conjecture and is open in general.

323283.title: Convexity of the persistence exponent for fractionally integrated Lévy processes
323283.statement:
For each $\beta\ge0$, let $\theta(\beta)$ denote the persistence exponent of a $\beta$-fractionally integrated Lévy process, when defined. **The convexity conjecture.** The function

$$
\beta\mapsto\theta(\beta)
$$

is convex decreasing.

The paper notes that existence is itself not established for every parameter range, and presents this shape property as a conjecture.

323647.title: Finite-type conjecture for linear LP algebras
323647.statement:
A **linear LP algebra** is an LP algebra whose exchange polynomials are linear in the relevant cluster variables, allowing the coefficients and constant terms described in the paper. **Finite-type conjecture.** Every linear LP algebra is of finite type.

This would extend the finite-type phenomenon from graph LP algebras to arbitrary linear LP algebras. The source gives no proof or resolution.

324468.title: The $K_n'$ formulation of the Lonely Runner Conjecture
324468.statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $K_n'$ be the obstruction parameter defined in the paper, and let $\kappa(n)$ be the quantity satisfying

$$
K_n'=1-2\kappa(n).
$$

**The $K_n'$ formulation.**

$$
K_n'=\frac{n-1}{n+1}
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This is stated as equivalent to the Lonely Runner Conjecture through the relation above. It remains open in general.

324595.title: Vanishing of negative semi-topological K-groups for smooth proper dg-categories
324595.statement:
Let $T$ be a smooth proper dg-category over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\mathbf{K}^{\mathrm{st}}_i(T)$ denote its semi-topological K-groups. **Vanishing conjecture.**

$$
\mathbf{K}^{\mathrm{st}}_i(T)=0\qquad\text{for all }i<0.
$$

This is presented as a generalization of a known vanishing theorem for smooth proper dg-categories. The source gives no resolution status, so the conjecture remains open.

324859.title: Keel's strict nefness conjecture for surfaces over finite fields
324859.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over $\bar{\mathbb F}_p$, and let $L$ be a **strictly nef** line bundle on $X$, meaning that $L\cdot C>0$ for every irreducible curve $C\subset X$. **Keel's conjecture.** The line bundle $L$ is ample. This is Keel's question; by the Nakai–Moishezon criterion and Artin's theorem, it is equivalent to the non-existence of strictly nef line bundles with $L^2=0$.

325093.title: Greene's doubly primitive conjecture for knots in $S^1 \times S^2$
325093.statement: Let $K$ be a knot in $S^1 \times S^2$ and suppose that a longitudinal surgery on $K$ produces a lens space. **Greene's conjecture.** The knot $K$ is doubly primitive. This is the broader replacement for Greene's original Berge-Gabai-only conjecture and is presented as the main conjecture of the paper; the authors propose families intended to account for all such knots.

326035.title: Uniform boundedness conjecture for Sierpinski gasket sampling functions
326035.statement: Let $\psi_m$ denote a sampling function on level $m$ of the Sierpinski gasket. **Uniform boundedness conjecture.** The sampling functions are uniformly bounded by some constant, numerically around $1.3$, for all $m$. This conjecture is motivated by numerical calculations and is consistent with the corresponding behavior of sampling functions on the real line.
